userStories.title: Classify provider API-error messages by HTTP status
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Classify anchored provider API-error messages by their status on both pi-client error paths instead of retrying deterministic 4xx as transport faults.

**Motivation** — The observed retries logged `kind: "transport"`: a 400 that can never succeed (the provider's "model trains on request data" policy) was retried 2x by the native adapter times 3 same-agent attempts, about 12 calls and 75 s per review call; 84 retry events in two runs on one day.

**Approach** — The prefix is a provider name: a letter or digit, then up to 79 characters from letters, digits, space, `.`, `_` and `-` (no colon, so `Request failed: x API error (400)` is not read), then ` API error (`, three digits starting 4 or 5, then `): `. In regex form: `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 ._-]{0,79} API error \(([45]\d\d)\): `. It matches `opencode-go`, `Azure OpenAI`, `github-copilot` and `Mistral`. The existing two shapes keep working. In `classifyThrown` the thrown value's own `status` / `statusCode` / `response.status` (`thrownStatus`) wins, then the message. A throw whose message matches no shape stays `transport`, as before (connection reset, DNS failure). The kind is `classifyProviderError(status, message)` on both paths, so 503 is `overloaded` and 500 is `transport`.

Extend `statusFromSdkMessage` with the `<provider> API error (<status>): ` shape (the provider-name grammar above), which also fixes the stream error event path in `pi-client.ts`, and make `classifyThrown` fall back to it when the thrown value has no status property, so a 4xx is `bad-request` / `auth` / `rate-limit` / `quota` on both paths and is never retried as a transport fault. Preserve ProtocolSetupError, cause, full message, retry-after and existing classification refinements.

**Scope** — In: errors.ts parser and throw classification plus regressions through both pi-client stream seams. Out: US-003's adapter swap policy, US-004's no-work close and new retry configuration.
- Caching a provider's credential failure across runs: `fail-auth` already parks the provider for the whole run (`cooldown: "run"`); the #2877 report of a second 401 was a second run, ruled not a defect 2026-11-12.
- Recovering a status quoted in the middle of an error message: only the anchored prefix shapes are read. The extended parser is reached from pi-client.ts:419 (stream error event); classifyThrown is reached from pi-client.ts:463 (stream catch). Enter each path through the pi client stream in seam tests.

**Interface** — `statusFromSdkMessage(message: string | undefined): number | undefined`; `classifyThrown(cause: unknown): ProtocolError`. No signature changes. No `thrownStatus` -> `statusFromSdkMessage(message)`; when that yields a status the kind is `classifyProviderError(status, message)` and the error carries `status`; otherwise `transport` as before. Update packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client-error-status.test.ts by adding an `opencode-go API error (400): {...}` error-event row with no observed status, expecting kind `bad-request` and status 400; existing rows are unchanged.

userStories.title: Require a left boundary before sk- secrets
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Stop the shared redactor from interpreting the sk- suffix of ordinary identifiers as an API key while retaining real-key masking.

**Motivation** — `SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS` openai entry `/sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/g` (`packages/nax-agent/src/internal/redact.ts:44`) has no left boundary, so `task-...` became `ta[REDACTED]` 62 times in audit files.

**Approach** — the openai pattern becomes `/(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/g`. Anchor the openai entry of `SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS` with `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])` so `task-...`, `disk-...` and similar words are not redacted, while a real `sk-` key at the start, after whitespace or punctuation or inside quotes still is.

**Scope** — In: the openai entry in packages/nax-agent/src/internal/redact.ts and additive boundary regressions in test/unit/logger/redact.test.ts. Out: US-008's PRD scan/warnings and US-001's provider-status classification; do not alter other secret patterns, key-based masking, replacement markers, recursive behavior or the exported pattern table's shape. Existing redactor tests remain unchanged: no existing case constructs an sk- run preceded by a letter, digit, _ or -.

**Interface** — `SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS` openai entry: baseline `{ kind: "openai", re: /sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/g }`; target `{ kind: "openai", re: /(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/g }`. The consumer signature stays `redactSecrets<T>(input: T): T`. Preserve global-regex resetting and Node-compatible source.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] redactSecrets("test:task-abcdefghijklmnopqrst") returns "test:task-abcdefghijklmnopqrst" unchanged.
[unit] redactSecrets("chat-task-abcdefghijklmnopq/workflow") returns the input unchanged.
[unit] redactSecrets("disk-0123456789abcdefgh") returns the input unchanged.
[unit] redactSecrets("my_sk-0123456789abcdefgh") returns the input unchanged, because _ before sk- is a word character.
[unit] redactSecrets("sk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa") returns a string that no longer holds "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa".
[unit] redactSecrets("key: sk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa") redacts the key that follows ': '.
[unit] redactSecrets('"sk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"') redacts the key inside double quotes.
[unit] redactSecrets("token=sk-proj-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa") returns a string that no longer holds "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa".
[unit] redactSecrets("(sk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa)") redacts the key that follows '('.
[unit] redactSecrets("line one\nsk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa") redacts the key that follows a newline.
[unit] redactSecrets("keys/sk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa") redacts the key that follows '/'.
[unit] redactSecrets("a,sk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa") redacts the key that follows ','.

routing.reasoning: One regex entry changes, but credential/token redaction is security-critical and requires strict three-session TDD.

userStories.title: Swap adapter errors after the same-agent retry lane
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make fail-adapter-error eligible for fallback after its existing same-agent retry even when onQualityFailure is disabled.

**Motivation** — An implementer hop got `{"detail":"Bad Request"}` (kind `bad-request`, outcome `fail-adapter-error`).

**Approach** — `after-retry-lane` already exists (`fail-timeout`, `fail-spin`, `fail-invalid-tool-call`): `trySameAgentRetry` spends the `adapter-error` lane first, then `decideSwap` swaps, subject to `fallback.enabled` and the hop cap. This reverses the earlier rule, pinned in `test/unit/agents/native/errors.test.ts`, that a malformed request (`bad-request`) and a context overflow stay on the failing agent unless `onQualityFailure` is on: user ruling 2026-11-12, a provider-side 400 is better served by another agent than by gates on an empty branch. `fail-quality` and `fail-unknown` stay `quality-gated`.

Change the `fail-adapter-error` row of `POLICIES` to `swap: "after-retry-lane"` (a design change: a `bad-request` and a context overflow now swap without `onQualityFailure`). Other fields unchanged. The manager already retries before decideSwap; add no new retry-lane flag, state machine, configuration or duplicate gate. Preserve the early abort exit.

**Scope** — In: failure-policy.ts and regressions through decideSwap and AgentManager.runWithFallback. Out: US-001's provider-message parsing and US-004's story close behavior.
- Rewording the `fail-adapter-error: same-agent retry with fresh session` log line or its `retriable` field.
- Marking `fail-quality` or `fail-unknown` swap-eligible without `onQualityFailure`.

**Required test updates (in scope)** — Rename/update the native errors tests 'an overflow is declined by default, like any fail-adapter-error' and 'a genuinely malformed request stays declined' to assert swaps after the retry lane, reflecting the explicit design change.

**Interface** — `POLICIES["fail-adapter-error"]`: target `swap: "after-retry-lane"`; other fields unchanged. Read-only consumer: `decideSwap(failure, hopsSoFar, fallback): SwapDecision`. Keep `sameAgentRetry: "adapter-error"`, `cooldown: "none"`, `cooldownScope: "model"` and terminalBackoff as today. Demonstrate the claude-to-codex manager seam with fallback enabled, onQualityFailure false and unsuccessful claude hops, not just a pure policy assertion.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] failurePolicyFor("fail-adapter-error").swap returns "after-retry-lane".
[unit] failurePolicyFor("fail-adapter-error").sameAgentRetry is still "adapter-error".
[unit] failurePolicyFor("fail-adapter-error").cooldown is still "none".
[unit] failurePolicyFor("fail-adapter-error").cooldownScope is still "model".
[unit] failurePolicyFor("fail-quality").swap is still "quality-gated".
[unit] failurePolicyFor("fail-unknown").swap is still "quality-gated".
[unit] decideSwap(toAdapterFailure({ kind: "bad-request" }), 0, { enabled: true, onQualityFailure: false, maxHopsPerStory: 2 }) returns { swap: true }, not quality-failure-declined.
[unit] decideSwap(toAdapterFailure({ kind: "context-overflow" }), 0, { enabled: true, onQualityFailure: false, maxHopsPerStory: 2 }) returns { swap: true } with the same fallback config.
[unit] decideSwap with a fail-quality failure and the same fallback config still returns { swap: false, reason: "quality-failure-declined" }.
[unit] decideSwap with a fail-adapter-error failure and fallback.enabled false returns { swap: false, reason: "fallback-disabled" }.
[unit] decideSwap with a fail-adapter-error failure and hopsSoFar equal to the configured hop cap returns { swap: false, reason: "hop-cap-reached" }.

[integration] AgentManager.runWithFallback with agent.fallback { enabled: true, map: { claude: ["codex"] }, onQualityFailure: false }, where every claude attempt fails with { category: "quality", outcome: "fail-adapter-error", retriable: false } and codex succeeds, dispatches codex after the claude attempts.
[integration] In that claude-to-codex fallback setup, AgentManager.runWithFallback returns result.success true.
[integration] In the same setup with an aborted run signal, an aborted fail-adapter-error hop is still neither retried nor swapped.

routing.reasoning: The production change is one existing policy value; manager retry/swap ordering already exists, while the fresh-session retry/abort regressions retain the mandatory session-security strategy.

The test "a genuinely malformed request stays declined" now expects `decideSwap(toAdapterFailure({ kind: "bad-request" }), 0, fallback)` to return a swap, and is renamed to say a malformed request swaps after the retry lane (design change, user ruling 2026-11-12).

userStories.title: Close a failed first dispatch with no work before gates
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Close the story complete-gate-open without gates or review when its first implement phase ends in a dispatch failure with explicitly absent work.

**Motivation** — Its policy is `swap: "quality-gated"`, so with `onQualityFailure` off the swap was declined; the failure became a session finding (`story-steps.ts` `absorbTurn`), `implementStep` exited `worked`, and the gates ran against a branch with no implementation.

**Approach** — The check is the existing optional story-loop step `steps.workProduced` (`workflow/story-loop.ts:60`; `buildStoryEnv` wires it to `storyWorkEvidence`). Absent means "work produced" and a throw is read as work, the same fail-open reading `runNoWorkLadder` uses (`workflow/no-work.ts`). The close mirrors the no-work ladder close: `closeAs` with state `complete-gate-open`, exit `"no-work"` (the graph routes `no-work` to `close`, skipping `evaluate`). Only the story's first implement turn is covered; a fix-round dispatch failure keeps today's session-finding path. The discriminator is `result.outcome` (the no-work ladder's last turn). An aborted run (`env.aborted?.()` true) never takes the new close: the stage's abort path handles it.

In `implementStep`, after the no-work ladder: when `result.outcome.failure` is set, the ladder did not close the story, the run is not aborted, and `env.steps.workProduced` is wired and resolves `false`, close the story `complete-gate-open` with reason `implementer dispatch failed: <failure>` and exit `"no-work"`. A missing or rejecting work check retains today's worked/session-finding path; a successful turn is not this failure path. Existing failure tests without workProduced remain on today's path.

**Scope** — In: implementStep's first implement phase, its conservative evidence reading, direct step behavior and runStoryLoop wiring. Out: US-003's fallback policy and US-005's summary counters, changes to storyWorkEvidence and changes to the stage's existing abort handling.
- A fix-round implementer dispatch that fails: it keeps today's session-finding path; only the story's first implement turn closes gate-open.

**Interface** — `implementStep(env: StoryLoopEnv, state: StoryLoopState): Promise<StepResult<StoryLoopState>>` stays unchanged; optional existing `workProduced?(): Promise<boolean>`. When `result.outcome.failure` is set, the ladder did not close, and the non-aborted work check resolves false, return `closeAs: { state: "complete-gate-open", reason: "implementer dispatch failed: <failure>" }` and exit `"no-work"`. Reuse the existing graph transition, rather than bypassing the story loop. The integration seam enters runStoryLoop and observes that gates and storyReview never run, with zero fix rounds.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With an implement turn returning { failure: 'Agent "native" failed: Bad Request', autoCommitted: false } and steps.workProduced resolving false, implementStep returns exit "no-work".
[unit] In the same failed-turn/no-work case, implementStep's patch carries closeAs.state "complete-gate-open".
[unit] In the same failed-turn/no-work case, closeAs.reason is 'implementer dispatch failed: Agent "native" failed: Bad Request'.
[unit] With the same failed turn and steps.workProduced resolving true, implementStep returns exit "worked".

[unit] With the same failed turn and steps.workProduced resolving true, implementStep's patch.pendingSession contains a finding whose issue is 'implementer session failed: Agent "native" failed: Bad Request'.
[unit] With the same failed turn and no steps.workProduced wired, implementStep returns exit "worked".
[unit] With the same failed turn and steps.workProduced rejecting, implementStep returns exit "worked".
[unit] With the same failed turn, steps.workProduced resolving false and env.aborted returning true, implementStep does not return a closeAs whose reason starts with 'implementer dispatch failed:'.
[unit] With a turn returning a reply and no failure, steps.workProduced resolving false does not produce a closeAs whose reason starts with 'implementer dispatch failed:'.

[integration] In the same run, runStoryLoop returns state "complete-gate-open".
[integration] In the same run, runStoryLoop returns rounds 0.
[integration] In the same run, env.steps.storyReview is never called.
[integration] runStoryLoop(env) with the same failed first turn and steps.workProduced resolving true calls env.steps.gates.
[integration] In that work-produced run, the next fix turn's findings include 'implementer session failed: Bad Request'.

userStories.title: Separate gate-open closures from completed run stories
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry story workflow end state to completion and count gate-open closures separately from completed work, with PRD-wide passed totals in the run summary.

**Motivation** — `workflow/stage.ts` always sets `ctx.agentResult.success = true`, so `pipeline/stages/completion.ts` logs "Story passed" and `handlePipelineSuccess` counts the story in `storiesCompleted` even when the story closed `complete-gate-open`: one run reported `storiesCompleted: 9, storiesFailed: 0` with `success: false` and a draft PR.

**Approach** — A story whose workflow end state is `complete-gate-open` is still marked `passed` in `prd.json` (user ruling 2026-11-12: reporting only, so a resume never re-runs it); it is not counted in `storiesCompleted` and is counted in a new `storiesGateOpen` on the "Feature execution completed" event, which also adds `storiesPassed`, the PRD-wide passed count (gate-open stories included, because their PRD status is `passed`). The new counters are optional fields read with `?? 0`, so the many test literals of `IterationResult` and the completion options keep compiling. A gate-open story still ends its iteration as terminal (`closeStoryIfTerminal`), so its sessions close. The progress line keeps status `passed` (`appendProgress` takes a `StoryStatus`, which has no gate-open value) and its text says `closed gate-open`.

The workflow stage sets ctx.workflowEndState to outcome.state after runStoryLoop, and to complete-gate-open on its non-aborted error path. Completion still calls markStoryPassed, but uses info message `Story closed gate-open` at stage completion and progress text ending `— closed gate-open` for that state. Ordinary/no-state contexts retain `Story passed`. handlePipelineSuccess excludes gate-open from storiesCompletedDelta and sets storiesGateOpenDelta on every success result. Keep the new count beside the completed count across every return/state copy, including dry-run and failure iterations, using zero defaults for missing inputs. No per-story batching redesign: workflow already rejects batches.

**Scope** — In: PipelineContext, workflow stage, completion stage, success result handling, iteration/executor/runner/completion plumbing, terminal session cleanup and Feature execution completed fields. Out: US-004's new dispatch-failure close, US-006's interrupt summary, US-007's push verdict and changes to resume selection.
- Changing a `complete-gate-open` story's `prd.json` status away from `passed`: ruled out 2026-11-12 (reporting only), so a resume never re-runs it.
- The `story:completed` event's `passed: true` for a gate-open story (hook and reporter payloads): only the log line and the run counters change.

**Interface** — `PipelineContext` gains optional `workflowEndState?: StoryState` (`StoryState` from workflow/types.ts:170). `PipelineSuccessResult` gains optional `storiesGateOpenDelta?: number`, set on every success result. The iteration result and executor chain gains an optional `storiesGateOpen?: number` / `storiesGateOpenDelta?: number` beside each `storiesCompleted` / `storiesCompletedDelta`, read with `?? 0`; `closeStoryIfTerminal` treats `storiesCompletedDelta > 0 || (storiesGateOpenDelta ?? 0) > 0` as terminal. Propagate through execution/iteration-runner.ts (dry-run/success/failure results), execution/dry-run.ts, execution/executor-types.ts, execution/unified-executor.ts, execution/unified-executor-dispatch-phases.ts (all early exits), execution/runner-execution.ts, execution/runner-completion.ts, execution/lifecycle/run-completion.ts (`RunCompletionOptions`) and execution/runner.ts. Feature execution completed data adds `storiesGateOpen` (0 when absent) and `storiesPassed: finalCounts.passed`.

The integration seam starts with workflow outcome production, consumes context state in completion/result handling and reaches the summary through the unified-executor chain. Test terminal session closure as well as the two-story complete/gate-open totals. Existing optional-field literals must retain their behavior without being mass-updated to conceal absent-field handling.

[unit] After runStoryLoop resolves with state "complete", the workflow stage leaves ctx.workflowEndState equal to "complete".
[unit] When runStoryLoop throws and the run is not aborted, the workflow stage leaves ctx.workflowEndState equal to "complete-gate-open".

[unit] The completion stage, for that gate-open story, logs info "Story closed gate-open" under stage completion and does not log "Story passed".

userStories.title: Read live PRD counters in interrupt summaries
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Report PRD-wide passed/failed counts from the live status-writer PRD when a run is interrupted, including safe setup-time fallbacks.

**Motivation** — "Feature execution terminated" (`execution/crash-writer.ts`) reports `storiesCompleted: 0` after an interrupt because `runner.ts` assigns its counter only after execution returns; a resumed run's `run.complete` counts only that session's stories.

**Approach** — "Feature execution terminated" reads the PRD the executor last loaded: the runner's own `prd` is the setup copy, and the unified executor replaces `state.prd` with a fresh `loadPRD` after each story, so the only live copy reachable from the crash handler is the one `StatusWriter.setPrd` receives each iteration. The event reports `storiesCompleted` and `storiesPassed` (both the PRD passed count) and `storiesFailed` (the PRD failed count).

Each runner crash getter reads `setupResult?.statusWriter.currentPrd() ?? prd` through setupResult, as getTotalCost does, because the destructured statusWriter const is not yet initialized when a signal arrives during setup. When a PRD exists, getStoriesCompleted/getStoriesPassed use countStories(...).passed and getStoriesFailed uses .failed. With no PRD, getStoriesCompleted falls back to the runner's own counter and getStoriesPassed/getStoriesFailed return 0. If setupResult is not available, the setup PRD or zero fallback must be safe without a temporal-dead-zone exception. No disk reload is needed.

**Scope** — In: StatusWriter getter, RunCompleteContext getter fields, writeRunComplete payload, runner closures and the setup/crash-recovery forwarding contracts needed to connect them. Out: US-005's normal-completion gate-open count, US-007's workflow success rule and changes to status persistence.
- Logging an interrupt during session open at a level other than error ("Story failed").

**Interface** — `StatusWriter` gains `currentPrd(): PRD | null`, returning the PRD last passed to setPrd. `RunCompleteContext` gains optional `getStoriesFailed?: () => number` and `getStoriesPassed?: () => number`; Feature execution terminated data adds storiesFailed and storiesPassed, 0 when a getter is absent. Preserve the existing optional getStoriesCompleted contract. Forward both new getters through RunnerSetupOptions/runSetupPhase in execution/runner-setup.ts, setupRun options/installation in execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts and CrashRecoveryContext in execution/crash-recovery.ts so installSignalHandlers/writeRunComplete receive them.

StatusWriter.currentPrd is produced and consumed in this same story. Tests must reach the runner's actual crash-context closures with a different live PRD than its setup PRD, plus a signal during awaited setup, rather than testing only countStories or a hand-built final log.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] StatusWriter.currentPrd() returns null before any setPrd call.
[unit] After setPrd(a) then setPrd(b), StatusWriter.currentPrd() returns b.
[unit] writeRunComplete with getStoriesCompleted returning 8, getStoriesPassed returning 8 and getStoriesFailed returning 1 writes Feature execution terminated data with storiesCompleted 8.
[unit] In that writeRunComplete call, Feature execution terminated data contains storiesPassed 8.
[unit] In that writeRunComplete call, Feature execution terminated data contains storiesFailed 1.
[unit] writeRunComplete with no getStoriesPassed and no getStoriesFailed writes storiesPassed 0.
[unit] writeRunComplete with no getStoriesPassed and no getStoriesFailed writes storiesFailed 0.

userStories.title: Make failed pushes fail the workflow verdict
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Distinguish a failed push from intentional local-only publishing and propagate that failure to workflow verdicts and run.complete success.

**Motivation** — A push rejected by the forge (GitHub push protection GH013 on a secret-shaped test string the run auto-committed into `prd.json`) ended `outcome: "local-only", passed: true`; the run looked green and published nothing.

**Approach** — `featurePassed` (`approval.ts:135`) stays a stories-and-gates verdict; `publishStep` ANDs it with "no push failure", because the run's `success` comes from the record's `passed` (`workflow-end-report.ts:223` -> `run-completion-phases.ts:395`), not from `buildVerdict`. `buildVerdict` gets the same clause for `nax workflow status` and chat. `publishStep` always writes `pushFailed` (true or false), like `approval` and `ciDetail`, because the record merges patches (`stage-env.ts:168`) and a `--publish-only` re-publish resumes the prior record (`publish-only.ts:31`): a successful re-publish after a failed push must clear the flag. The finished-at-HEAD path (`feature.ts:239-245`) is unchanged: it only accepts `ready`, `draft` or `pushed` records, which never carry a push failure once the flag is cleared.

Set pushFailed only on failed-push returns from both pushMode and prMode, and log `Push failed — the feature ends local-only` at error level with the rejection in error. A publish:none or no-forge local-only outcome is not a push failure and leaves the stories-and-gates verdict unchanged. Do not special-case GH013 text; all non-aborted rejected pushes take this failure path. Preserve abort propagation and existing CI/readiness behavior.

**Scope** — In: PublishOutcome/WorkflowFeatureRecord flag, failed-push returns, existing push log level, publishStep patch clearing and passed composition, buildVerdict guard and end-report integration. Out: US-005/US-006's story counters, US-008's planner warning, changes to featurePassed, new push-protection bypasses, or finished-at-HEAD/publish-only eligibility changes.

**Interface** — `PublishOutcome` gains optional `pushFailed?: true`, set on the failed-push returns of pushMode and prMode. `WorkflowFeatureRecord` gains optional `pushFailed?: boolean`. `publishStep` always writes `pushFailed: out.pushFailed === true`; when it is true, `passed` is false, otherwise passed is as today. `buildVerdict(rec: WorkflowFeatureRecord): WorkflowVerdict | undefined` makes workflowPassed also false when `rec.pushFailed === true`.

The integration seam is publish -> publishStep -> persisted passed:false -> runEndPhaseReported/CloseInput -> Feature execution completed success:false. Test successful re-publish on a prior pushFailed:true record to prove merge-safe clearing. Older records with no flag retain existing behavior.

userStories.title: Stamp plan timestamps and warn on secret-shaped story text
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Generate plan timestamps in code and warn, without mutation or refusal, when persisted PRD story strings match shared secret-redaction patterns.

**Motivation** — The planner prompt asks the model for `createdAt` (`plan-builder.ts:418`) and `validatePlanOutput` (`prd/schema.ts:163`) trusts it; PRDs were dated weeks in the future.

**Approach** — For each story (only the stories in `args.scope` when a scope is given), every string in `title`, `description` and `acceptanceCriteria` is passed through `redactSecrets` (`@nathapp/nax-agent/internal`, as `config/secret-scan.ts` imports it); a string that comes back changed is a hit. Hits are warned, never redacted and never fatal (user ruling 2026-11-12: specs about redaction quote fake keys legitimately). `findPrdSecretShapes` is exported from the `src/prd/index.ts` barrel.

`validatePlanOutput` takes an optional `now` and ignores the model's `createdAt`/`updatedAt`; the planner prompt stops asking for them. Create `prd/secret-shapes.ts` with `findPrdSecretShapes`, exported from `src/prd/index.ts`; `finalizeAndWritePrd` warns once per hit with the story id and field and writes the PRD unchanged. Visit stories in their existing order and fields in title, description, acceptance-criteria-index order; return one result per changed string, not per token. Scan the finalized PRD immediately before args.writeFile, passing args.scope. Log metadata, not the candidate string. If redactSecrets/findPrdSecretShapes throws, catch at the persistence boundary, warn once that the secret-shape scan could not run, and still write the PRD. No new regex catalog or config setting.

**Scope** — In: schema.ts timestamp normalization, removal of timestamp keys from the planner's displayed schema, new PRD scanner/barrel export, advisory persistence warnings and their seam tests. Out: US-002's shared redactor boundary, US-007's failed-push verdict, scanning unrelated PRD fields and rewriting existing execution PRDs' timestamps.
- Refusing `nax plan` on a secret-shaped PRD string, or redacting it: ruled out 2026-11-12; the plan only warns.

**Integration boundary** — Keep all dependencies empty per the binding structure; reuse the shared redactor rather than independently fixing its task- false positive here.

**Interface** — `validatePlanOutput(raw: unknown, feature: string, branch: string, now?: Date): PRD`; createdAt and updatedAt are both `(now ?? new Date()).toISOString()`, whatever the model wrote. The createdAt and updatedAt lines are removed from the schema the model is shown. New `findPrdSecretShapes(prd: PRD, scope?: ReadonlySet<string>): PrdSecretShape[]` in packages/nax/src/prd/secret-shapes.ts with `interface PrdSecretShape { readonly storyId: string; readonly field: string }`; field is `"title"`, `"description"` or `"acceptanceCriteria[<index>]"`. With a scope, only stories whose id is in it are scanned. `finalizeAndWritePrd(args: PersistPrdArgs): Promise<string>` keeps its signature; before the final write it calls findPrdSecretShapes(prd, args.scope) and logs one `getLogger().warn("plan", ...)` per hit; the written PRD is unchanged. `redactSecrets<T>(input: T): T` remains read-only. Add packages/nax/test/unit/prd/secret-shapes.test.ts and extend existing schema, prompt and persistence tests; use the existing injectable persistence seam for the throwing-scan integration case.

Grounding and delivery contract
This is an enhancement/bug-fix feature in an existing Bun-workspace TypeScript monorepo, closing #2877, #2879 and #2882. The codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session; findings below were grounded using direct source reads and targeted text searches at the supplied repository root. Preserve exactly US-001 through US-008, their package workdirs and empty dependency arrays. There are no new configuration keys, package dependencies, releases or changes required in nax-agent-acp. The individual stories remain independently scoped even where their behaviors compose. Read docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:17 for the repository's conventions, dependency injection, testing and logging references. Package-specific AGENTS.md instructions govern implementation. Only the PRD is being authored by this planning task; no implementation or tests have been executed.

US-001: provider errors and transport retry
packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/errors.ts:23 currently recognizes only /^([45]\d\d):? (\{|status code)/. classifyHttpError at :11 distinguishes auth (401/403), quota (402), rate-limit (429), overloaded (503/529), other 4xx bad-request and other 5xx transport. classifyProviderError at :176 preserves message-aware context-overflow and quota refinements; reuse it, rather than adding a second classification table. thrownStatus at :247 already reads status/statusCode/response.status and validates a finite number; preserve precedence and this helper's behavior. classifyThrown at :292 currently returns transport immediately for a status-less throw; only fall back to the anchored SDK-message parser after thrownStatus yields undefined. Preserve ProtocolSetupError handling, message, cause and retry-after handling. packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts:419 invokes statusFromSdkMessage for error events when observed status is absent; :463 invokes classifyThrown in the stream catch. Therefore one parser change covers two distinct stream seams, and tests must enter both through createPiProtocol.stream, not merely call the pure helper. An observed response status remains authoritative on the error-event path. packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/retry.ts:35 and :91 permit only transport retry before the first event; classification changes remove deterministic provider 4xx from that lane without changing retry policy. A 500 stays transport, 503 stays overloaded and a socket/DNS failure remains transport. Existing tests: packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/errors.test.ts:35 and :300 cover parsing and throws; packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client-error-status.test.ts:60 contains the table to extend, :91 pins observed-status precedence and :107 exercises retry through a fake pi dependency. packages/nax-agent/src/internal/redact.ts:43 exports SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS; :44 has the unbounded openai /sk-/ entry. Add only the specified negative lookbehind; do not replace all token matching or key-aware masking. redactString at :137 resets each global regex lastIndex before replacement; redactSecrets at :153 recursively applies masking. packages/nax/src/agents/retry/failure-policy.ts:147 assigns fail-adapter-error the adapter-error lane, quality-gated swap, no cooldown, model cooldownScope and terminalBackoff false. packages/nax/src/workflow/story-steps.ts:332 implements only the first implement node. It calls runNoWorkLadder, absorbs the final result.outcome, and currently only closes when result.closed is true. packages/nax/src/workflow/no-work.ts:84 treats outcome.failure as NOT a no-work turn, explaining why dispatch errors currently proceed to evaluation. :70 reads an absent or throwing work check as work produced, logging a safe warning on a throw. packages/nax/src/workflow/stage.ts:52 gets the story-loop outcome but :81 always assigns a successful agent result; the catch at :62 persists complete-gate-open without carrying that state to completion. Add optional PipelineContext.workflowEndState using StoryState from packages/nax/src/workflow/types.ts:170. Set it from the loop outcome, and to complete-gate-open on non-aborted error paths; retain success=true and PRD passed semantics. packages/nax/src/pipeline/stages/completion.ts:139 marks stories passed, :144 logs Story passed, :151 appends progress with StoryStatus passed, and :165 emits story:completed passed=true. packages/nax/src/execution/status-writer.ts:80 stores _prd=null and :157 replaces it in setPrd. Expose currentPrd(): PRD | null without cloning or disk reload. packages/nax/src/execution/unified-executor-dispatch-phases.ts:191 reloads the PRD when dirty and :194 passes that replacement to the writer each iteration. Reading runner's setup PRD cannot recover that updated reference. packages/nax/src/execution/runner.ts:200 initializes its local completed count, :209 declares prd before setup, :216 declares setupResult, :247 already uses setupResult?.statusWriter for live cost, :252 exposes only the stale local completed count, and :262 destructures statusWriter after awaited setup. packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts:41 defines PublishOutcome; :95 pushBranch logs a rejected push as warn at :104 and returns a reason; pushMode at :437 and prMode at :460 currently return local-only with skipped CI on push failure but no discriminating flag. The new getter method must be available on relevant StatusWriter test doubles when those paths are exercised, while optional counter/getter fields keep old result/option literals compatible. No backfill of historical run logs or credential-failure caching is requested. Preserve exact anchored provider grammar and property precedence so quoted or unrelated text cannot acquire a status. Avoid disclosing token text in scan warnings; intentional fake examples remain unchanged on disk. Use shared fixture/mocking helpers and existing _deps seams, with package-local commands (vitest through bun run test in nax-ai, targeted path-based bun:test in nax/nax-agent). Every regression test must be demonstrated failing against the old implementation before the fix counts; no live paid-provider calls are needed for this feature.
